what_it_is.text: Tongatapu is the main island of Tonga and the site of its capital Nukuʻalofa; about 260 km2, built of flat coral limestone, with roughly 70% of the country's population.
Nukuʻalofa is the centre of commerce and government and home of the royal family in the South Pacific's only monarchy; Tonga was never colonised.

distinctive_fact.text: Ha'amonga 'a Maui is a coral-limestone trilithon built around 1200 AD, and Mu'a was the seat of the Tu'i Tonga kings, whose terraced langi tombs (1200-1800 AD) survive.
The Fanga'uta and Fangakakau lagoons were declared a Natural Reserve in 1974 and are breeding grounds for birds and fish.

draws.text: Ancient Tongan royal history: Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon and Lapaha/Mu'a langi royal tombs
Rugged south coast: Mapu 'a Vaea blowholes (best at high tide) and Hufangalupe natural land bridge
Day trips to island resorts Pangaimotu, Fafa or 'Atata by ferry; Pangaimotu has a half-sunken wreck to snorkel (about T$20 return)
Tongan culture: feast and dance shows (Ancient Tonga, 'Oholei Beach), Talamahu Market, Sunday church singing
Swimming with humpback whales is also offered from Tongatapu in season (June-November)

tips.text: Sunday: almost all businesses, shops and services close; work, sport and loud activity are discouraged; some hotels/restaurants stay open. Arrange Sunday food with your hotel, especially if arriving Saturday.

Driving needs a valid home licence plus a Tongan visitor's driving permit (issued at Nukuʻalofa Police HQ or via rental agencies); drive on the left, low speed limits (50 km/h on most of the island), few road signs.
Buses run from the Nukuʻalofa seafront concourse with no posted timetables and are unreliable after about 15:30; flag them down at the roadside.
Tonga is cash-oriented; ATMs and banks are mainly in Nukuʻalofa, cards work only at major tourist spots; currency is the pa'anga (TOP).
Dress modestly; people have been arrested for walking around topless.
Airport (Fuaʻamotu, TBU) is about 30 minutes from Nukuʻalofa; taxi usually T$50, shuttle T$10 per Wikivoyage (2019, price unverified now).

best_months.reason: Cool dry season May-October (peak July-October, best June-September), less humid; humpback season July-October; Heilala Festival in July. November-April is hot, wet, cyclone season.

tongatapu.seasonal: Humpback whales June-November (Tonga Tourism says calves arrive July-October); peak tourist season July-October; Heilala Festival in July; secondary peak at Christmas/New Year. Cyclone season November-April.
tongatapu.coordinates_note: Centre per placement -21.17,-175.18 (pending pin). Wikipedia island centre -21.21139,-175.15306.

what_it_is.text: Vava'u is a group of more than 50 (tourism board: 61) raised-limestone and coral islands about 250 km north of Tongatapu; main town Neiafu on 'Utu Vava'u.
Neiafu's Port of Refuge Harbour is a yachting hub: over 500 yachts visit each winter sailing season (June-October).

distinctive_fact.text: A string of islands and reefs along the eastern edge shelters the group, and humpback whales come to these protected waters to give birth; visibility is said to reach 30-40 m.
Vava'u is a major producer of high-quality vanilla.

draws.text: Swim with humpback whales: mothers and calves, season June/July to November (tourism board: July-October); Tonga is one of few places where this is still allowed; use only licensed operators
Sailing and island hopping among sheltered anchorages, hidden coves, beaches; yacht charters and day tours (about $50 pp)
Snorkel and dive: coral gardens, Swallows Cave (snorkelling), Mariner's Cave (underwater-tunnel entrance), shipwrecks
Game fishing for marlin, sailfish, tuna, giant trevally
Land: Mt Talau National Park walk (about 1 km trail, harbour views), 'Ene'io Botanical Garden, vanilla plantations, kayaking

tips.text: Book only licensed whale operators listed by Tonga Tourism; peak July-October needs activity and accommodation booked in advance.

Getting there: international flights land at Tongatapu; scheduled flights from Nadi (Fiji) to Vava'u were twice weekly per Wikivoyage; Lulutai Airlines is the only domestic airline, Tongatapu-Vava'u flights; a ferry (MV 'Otuanga'afa) also runs.
Sunday: shops and most services close, loud activity discouraged; some hotels/restaurants open. Dress modestly; carry cash, especially on outer islands.
Women do not drink kava at the local kava bars (Wikivoyage lists kava as for men only); an etiquette point, unverified beyond that note.

best_months.reason: Whales June/July-November (peak July-September/October); cooler, drier trade-wind season May-September for sailing; summer Nov-April humid with thunderstorms and cyclones.

vavau.seasonal: Humpback season (Wikivoyage June-November; tourism board July-October, prime July-September); yacht season June-October; cyclone season Nov-April.

what_it_is.text: 'Eua is a hilly, non-volcanic island of 87 km2 (pop. 4,903 in 2021) just southeast of Tongatapu, formerly Middelburg Island; highest point 312 m.
Tonga's oldest island geologically, with cliffs, caves, sinkholes and rainforest; billed as an adventurer's, hiker's island.

distinctive_fact.text: A seven-minute flight from Tongatapu is one of the world's shortest commercial flights.
'Eua National Park is Tonga's only forest national park (4.51 km2); its main attraction is the Big Ovava Tree, said to be over 800 years old.

draws.text: Hiking: marked trails through 'Eua National Park, coastal walk, cliffs, caves, chasms; Tonga's best hiking per tourism board
Coastal lookouts and rock features: Lakufa'anga Cliff, Rockgarden Cliffs, Li'angahuo 'a Maui natural stone bridge, Matalanga 'a Maui pothole, Ha'aluma Beach swim
Caves incl. 'Ana 'Ahu with stalactites; diving a large underwater cavern about 30 m deep
Birdwatching for the rare red shining parrot (koki); humpbacks pass close to shore June/July-November

tips.text: Reach by Lulutai flight from Tongatapu (about 7 minutes) or a 2.5-3 hour ferry from Nukuʻalofa; check the schedule.
Getting around: rental cars, taxis and local buses on 'Eua; carry cash on outer islands; Sunday is a day of rest with most businesses closed.
Trails are crossed by cliffs and sinkholes; use well-marked trails (hazard advice unverified for specific tracks).

best_months.reason: Cool dry season May-October is better for hiking (peak July-October); humpbacks June/July-November; Nov-April hot, wet, cyclone season.

eua-island.seasonal: Humpback whales June/July-November pass close to shore; cyclone season Nov-April.
